Currently, there is some technical debt related to set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in in the valuation code, caused by the following:

  • In the definition of MonoidWithZeroHom.ValueGroup₀, the input is an arbitrary f : F with MonoidWithZeroHomClass F A B.
  • However, in the instance MonoidWithZeroHom.ValueGroup₀.instLinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero, the input is {f : A →*₀ B}.

As a result, the instance LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (ValueGroup₀ v) cannot be inferred automatically when v is a valuation. Only LinearOrderedCommGroupWithZero (ValueGroup₀ (v : _ →*₀ _)) can be inferred.

The inconsistency in the conditions is the root cause. We can fix this by either sticking to MonoidWithZeroHomClass consistently, or sticking to MonoidWithZeroHom consistently. I would like to know which approach is preferred, and what the general Mathlib principle is: should a general declaration use a HomClass or the homomorphism type itself?
The general rule is that definitions should be in terms of an actual FooHom instead of FooHomClass. This usually means that also most lemmas about these definitions should be in terms of FooHom.
See here for the relevant thread: #mathlib4 > Mathlib's morphism hierarchy @ 💬
Thanks! Then I'll open a PR to fix this tech debt.
I've tried this 10 days ago and it was not completely trivial, but maybe this is better now. I am almost sure this is the root cause of various erw.

I finished #36911 to fix it.

As a result, we are able to remove several erw and many set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in. The trade-off is that we now need to write an explicit coercion to MonoidWithZeroHom in ValueGroup₀. It now looks like ValueGroup₀ (Valued.v (R := R) : R →*₀ Γ₀).
I ran into this issue as well when looking into some leaky instances. Is it the concensus that we should go ahead with #36911 to fix this?
